To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. The problem of computing an optimal deterministic broadcast scheme for a graph is NP-hard.

the fastest deterministic broadcast schemes in radio networks with known topology can be constructed in polynomial time and that, unless a certain complexity theoretic conjecture fails, the polynomial time construction of a faster deterministic broadcast scheme is not possible.

the problem of finding a polynomially constructable broadcast scheme of length D in a radio network with n nodes is NP-hard, and that the problem is solvable in polynomial time for graphs of diameter $$O(\log n)$$.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: Is it possible to find polynomially constructible broadcast schemes of length $$\Theta (D)$$ for every graph G with diameter D?
the following questions: (1) What is the complexity of broadcasting in known topology radio networks?

the following questions: (i) Is there a polynomial algorithm which, given a network represented by a graph, constructs a broadcast scheme with the length of $$\mathcal O(D + \log ^\epsilon n)$$, $$\epsilon >0$$?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

for every n-node radio network, there is a polynomially constructable deterministic broadcast scheme of length at most $$\mathcal O(n^{1+\varepsilon} + D + \log^2n)$$, where $$\varepsilon$$ is any positive constant.

the length of a polynomially computable broadcast scheme for a graph of diameter D is either optimal or $$\mathcal {O}(D + n^{\varepsilon })$$ for a constant $$\varepsilon$$, where the latter is not optimal.
for deterministic broadcast, the best known scheme is the one of Gąsieńiec et al. with length O(D logn).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the deterministic polynomial construction of a broadcast scheme of optimal length for any graph G with diameter $$D(G)$$ is possible only when $$D(G) = \mathcal{O}\left(\sqrt{\log n}\right)$$.
we have designed a broadcast scheme which is polynomially constructible and has length $$\mathbf{O}(\mathbf{D} + \log ^{\mathbf{2}}\mathbf{n})$$, where the lower bound is tight.
we give an optimal deterministic polynomial time algorithm for constructing a broadcast scheme in a radio network, when the topology is known.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the topological information about a radio network can be efficiently exploited in designing broadcast algorithms, which is in contrast with the case when the network is unknown.
, for deterministic broadcasting, the topological structure of the network can be fully exploited.
in the case of known topologies, it is possible to achieve a better approximation factor than in the case of unknown topologies.
